business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Physical Arbitrage of Grade A Refined Copper Cathodes

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (Articles L.561-1 et seq.) and Ordonnance n° 2017-563 du 19 avril 2017 implementing EU AMLD5 for UBO register disclosure

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of identity and address for UBO
Articles of association or equivalent ownership documentation for UBO entity

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against FATF, EU, and French Tracfin PEP lists, OFAC SDN, UN sanctions, and domestic French sanctions lists

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: infogreffe.fr (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory use of French language in Latin script; no specific transliteration required
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Appeal to the President of the Tribunal de Commerce within 2 months of rejection notice, following administrative law procedures

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for SAS entities provided registered office address is verifiable and not a PO box only; commercial substance may be required for tax residency
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (5-10% for routine pre-incorporation checks; higher for suspicious filings)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence and UBO identification services
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for cross-border corporate setup in France

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name search and clearance via INPI/Infogreffe
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee plus administrative costs
Prevailing market rates for Hague Apostille processing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and virtual address setup

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff or prevailing market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), Book II, Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 (general company provisions), L.224-1 (share capital payment rules), L.225-2 (cash contribution escrow) as adapted, and L.227-1 to L.227-27 (Société par Actions Simplifiée regime covering incorporation, governance, and President's powers); implementing rules at R.123-30 et seq. (RCS filing); Decree No. 2021-300 of 18 March 2021 (electronic one-stop shop for business formalities).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court) acting as registrar of the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); filings are transmitted electronically through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (guichet-entreprises.fr) operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de création d'une personne morale (M0 form) submitted through the electronic single window, accompanied by the statuts constitutifs (articles of association) and the exhibits enumerated in the filing dossier.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS; the articles of association freely determine the capital amount. Cash subscriptions must be deposited into a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) held at a French credit institution or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the bank delivers a certificat du dépositaire des fonds which must accompany the RCS filing, and the funds are released only upon presentation of the issued Kbis. The articles may provide for staggered payment of cash subscriptions within five years, provided the full capital is subscribed at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the shareholders of [●] SAS, upon subscription of the entire share capital, hereby (i) approve and adopt the articles of association in the presented form; (ii) confirm that the share capital is fully subscribed and legally paid up, evidenced by the bank's certificate of deposit of funds; (iii) adopt the registered office at [address], authorizing the President to effectuate any future relocation with registry notification; and (iv) appoint [●] as the first President with full corporate powers to represent the Company, open bank accounts, and execute commercial contracts in France and abroad.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Articles of Association (Statuts Constitutifs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders acting under private signature (sous seing privé); a notary public is optional but required if real estate is contributed as an in-kind asset.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the articles of association in French. The document must contain the corporate name, legal form (SAS), registered office, corporate purpose (wholesale physical arbitrage of Grade A refined copper cathodes, HS 7403, ISIC 4662), share capital and classes of shares, duration (maximum 99 years), first President, and governance rules. Each founder must sign every page or the original signature page. No state filing is required at this step, but the finalised text determines all later filings.
required_dossiers: Draft statuts constitutifs
Valid passport or national ID of each founder
Proof of address and lawful use of the intended registered office (lease, domiciliation contract, or title deed)
Declaration of beneficial owners (BO declarations) as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a founder refuses to sign, remove the dissenting founder and adjust the share allocation by a fresh signature process. If any clause is legally non-compliant, revise and re-execute the articles before submission to the Greffe.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked Deposit of the Subscribed Cash Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any French credit institution (licensed bank) or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow account in the name of the company in formation, deposit the subscribed cash capital by wire transfer or certified cheque, and obtain the depositary certificate (certificat du dépositaire des fonds / attestation de blocage). The account remains frozen until the Kbis is issued; the certificate is a mandatory exhibit for the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening kit (KYC of founders and beneficial owners)
Executed statuts constitutifs or exact extract
Proof of corporate name availability check
Deposit instruction and record of the transferred funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the account on KYC grounds, the founders may invoke the 'droit au compte' procedure under Articles L.312-1 et seq. of the Code monétaire et financier before the Banque de France to compel the designation of a bank within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Incorporation Notice in a Legal Announcements Journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Accredited Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) of the department of the registered office, listed on the official registry of approved legal gazettes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the draft notice (avis de constitution) containing the corporate name, legal form, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, and identity of the first President. Obtain the attestation de parution from the JAL, which is a mandatory exhibit for the RCS registration. The publication should be completed before filing the M0 declaration.
required_dossiers: Draft notice of incorporation (avis de constitution) in French
Extract of the executed statuts constitutifs
Identity particulars of the President and statutory officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL rejects the notice for incomplete or inconsistent capital or officer details, correct the wording and republish immediately. If the notice is already printed with an error, publish an insertion rectificative (erratum) to cure the defect without invalidating the registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission of the Incorporation Dossier to the RCS via the Single Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (guichet-entreprises.fr) operated by the INPI, which routes the verified dossier to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office jurisdiction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic M0 declaration and attach all statutory exhibits: executed statuts, bank certificate of capital deposit, legal announcement attestation, proof of lawful use of the registered office, sworn non-conviction declarations of the President and statutory officers, ID of the President, and beneficial owner declarations. Authenticate electronically via FranceConnect or a certified identity provider, pay the registry fee, and keep the electronic receipt and dossier number for follow-up.
required_dossiers: M0 electronic declaration (création d'une personne morale)
Executed statuts constitutifs
Certificat du dépositaire des fonds (capital deposit certificate)
Attestation de parution au JAL
Justificatif de jouissance légale du local (lease, domiciliation contract, or property deed)
Déclaration sur l'honneur de non-condamnation of the President
Copy of valid identity document of the President
Declaration of beneficial owners (BO) as annexed to the filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a 'dossier incomplet' or query notice, respond through the portal within fifteen calendar days with the missing documents or a corrective filing. An unjustified refusal may be appealed to the President of the Commercial Court; alternatively, resubmit a fully cured electronic dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration and Issuance of the Kbis Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office jurisdiction, acting as registrar of the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon final validation, the Greffier enters the company in the RCS and issues the Kbis extract, which confers legal personality. The SIREN/SIRET identifiers are simultaneously allocated via INSEE. The company presents the Kbis to the bank to release the blocked funds and thereafter opens its permanent operating account and executes contracts in its own name.
required_dossiers: Approved electronic dossier transmitted by the Guichet unique
Payment confirmation of the statutory registry fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis contains errors, request rectification from the Greffier. If registration is refused, lodge an appeal before the President of the Commercial Court within fifteen days of notification, or file a new corrected dossier through the single window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) — residual authority for installations classées pour la protection de l'environnement (ICPE); no specific industrial licensing board is required for a pure wholesale trading mandate in non-ferrous metals.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No separate industrial or operational permit is prescribed for the wholesale distribution of Grade A refined copper cathodes. The ordinary trading authorization is the RCS registration as evidenced by the Kbis extract (Code de commerce, Article L.123-36). The 'revendeur de métaux' declaration under Article L.541-1 of the Code de commerce does not apply because the activity concerns primary refined metal, not scrap or second-hand metal.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) under the Préfecture, with coordination through the French EIA and ICPE registry.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full Environmental Impact Assessment for the pure wholesale trading activity. If the operator later operates a warehouse of finished goods above 500 tonnes, the site becomes subject to ICPE declaration (rubrique 1510, régime déclaratif) and the generic ICPE prescriptions, but still not a full EIA authorisation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the pure trading scope: no manufacturing process, no wastewater discharge point, and no VOC emission source are generated. Copper cathodes are not classified as dangerous goods under ADR. For any ICPE-declared warehouse, the generic ministerial prescriptions apply, including fire-water retention, waste segregation, and soil protection; commercial packaging obligations must be registered under the extended producer responsibility framework (Code de l'environnement, Articles L.541-1 et seq.).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: If offices or warehouses are operated, the premises must obtain fire safety conformity: for ERP (établissement recevant du public) category 5 premises, clearance is delivered by the local safety commission or SDIS; for ICPE warehouses, the DREAL declaration and the associated fire-resistance and means-of-escape requirements govern. On the occupational side, the employer must prepare the Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels (DUERP), affiliate to the statutory occupational health service (Service de Prévention et de Santé au Travail) by the first hire, and maintain first-aid, evacuation, and safety registers in accordance with the French Labour Code (Articles L.4121-1 et seq.).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministère de l'Économie et des Finances; tax portal: www.impots.gouv.fr; company registry: Guichet Unique (INPI) and Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); customs authority: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign entity forming a French SAS: (1) file incorporation formalities through the Guichet Unique (INPI) with articles, beneficial owner declarations, and registered office proof; (2) INSEE issues SIREN and SIRET; (3) DGFiP automatically assigns a French VAT ID if taxable operations are declared, otherwise the entity files form M0 with the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE). For non-established foreign entities making taxable supplies in France: register directly with the SIE using form M0 and supporting documents (certificate of incorporation, articles, proof of EU establishment, bank details, and VAT registration in home state); non-EU entities must appoint a French fiscal representative unless an exemption applies. EU distance sellers and certain B2C suppliers may use the One-Stop Shop (OSS/IOSS). Customs EORI number is obtained from DGDDI for import/export operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS) is subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) at the standard 25% rate (2025). No default pass-through. Territorial scope: French companies are taxable on worldwide profits, with treaty and foreign-branch relief. Not a tax-exempt zone. Eligible for parent-subsidiary regime and tax consolidation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a US-style check-the-box system. Available elections include: (i) tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) under Art. 223 A CGI for groups with 95% ownership; (ii) VAT group (assujettissement unique) under Art. 256 C CGI; (iii) limited option for partnership tax transparency for SAS under Art. 239 bis AB CGI subject to statutory conditions; (iv) simplified VAT regime where turnover thresholds are met. Anti-hybrid rules under Art. 205 I bis CGI apply; no domestic hybrid mismatch election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT registration threshold applies to non-established taxable persons making taxable supplies in France. Domestic franchise en base thresholds: €85,000 for goods and €37,500 for services (2024/2025). Intra-EU acquisitions threshold: €10,000. Wholesale trade in refined copper cathodes generally exceeds all thresholds and is fully VATable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is phasing in mandatory B2B e-invoicing and e-reporting through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) and accredited Partner Dematerialization Platforms (PDPs). Receiving obligation for all VAT-registered businesses from September 2026; issuing obligation for large and mid-sized companies from September 2026, and for SMEs/micro-enterprises from September 2027. Public-sector e-invoicing currently uses Chorus Pro. No general real-time fiscal clearance yet; structured formats, qualified electronic signatures/certificates, and lifecycle reporting are required. Non-compliance penalties include €15 per invoice (annual cap €15,000) and €250 per transmission failure.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods outside the EU are VAT-exempt at 0% under Art. 262-I CGI, provided the goods actually leave the EU and the exporter holds customs proof. Intra-EU supplies to VAT-registered customers are 0% under Art. 262-ter CGI with a valid customer VAT ID and VIES verification. Offshore services may be outside the scope of French VAT or zero-rated under place-of-supply rules. For Grade A refined copper cathodes, zero-rating requires a commercial invoice, transport document, and customs exit certification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: French customs export declaration (DAU/EX A) with MRN
Commercial invoice with VAT number and Incoterms
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR / LME warehouse warrant
Proof of exit from the EU (customs certification/stamp)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Failure to substantiate export zero-rating results in VAT reassessment at 20%, late interest of 0.20% per month (2.4% per year), and penalties of 40% for lack of evidence or 80% for fraudulent intent under Art. 1729 CGI. Criminal penalties for tax evasion under Art. 1741 CGI: up to 5 years imprisonment and a €500,000 fine; aggravated organized fraud: up to 7 years and €2,000,000. Customs penalties apply under the Code des douanes. Retrospective audit period is generally 3 years, extended to 10 years for concealed activity or offshore arrangements. France has no general statutory FX repatriation deadline; 180 days is a common contractual or documentary credit term.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) in coordination with the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) and the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) for banking supervision. The Banque de France is the central bank and the primary authority for monetary policy and financial stability, while the Treasury oversees foreign exchange regulations and balance-of-payments reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a member of the Eurozone; the euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. There are no exchange controls on capital movements, profit remittances, or dividend distributions, subject to compliance with EU anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing (CTF) regulations. However, all cross-border transfers exceeding €10,000 must be reported to the French customs and tax authorities for statistical and monitoring purposes. Profit remittance is unrestricted, but must be supported by audited financial statements and tax clearance certificates to avoid withholding tax issues.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds in France. Exporters may retain foreign currency in designated accounts (comptes en devises) and are free to use them for trade settlements or convert to euros at market rates. However, all export receipts must be declared to the Banque de France via the balance-of-payments reporting system (BOP) within 30 days of the transaction. The reporting is electronic and mandatory for all transactions exceeding EUR 12,500. No minimum conversion ratio applies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Fintech EMIs (Electronic Money Institutions) licensed under the EU PSD2 directive, such as Qonto, Shine, or Revolut Business, can provide multi-currency accounts and cross-border payment services. However, for high-value physical commodity trading (copper cathodes) involving documentary letters of credit (LC) and LME warrant transfers, traditional banks are preferred due to their established trade finance infrastructure, correspondent banking networks, and ability to handle complex documentary compliance. EMIs may face limitations in issuing or confirming LCs and may have lower transaction limits. Legal constraints include the need for the EMI to hold a valid ACPR license and to comply with French AML/KYC regulations, which are stringent for high-risk sectors like metals trading.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For corporate account opening, French banks generally require the physical presence of the legal representative (e.g., the SAS President) for the initial KYC interview and signature verification. However, some banks offer remote onboarding via video conferencing and electronic signature, subject to enhanced due diligence (EDD) and a risk-based approach. For a medium-risk entity like a copper trading company, banks may accept remote onboarding if the company provides notarized corporate documents, proof of address, and a detailed business plan. Nevertheless, a physical visit to the bank's branch or a notary in France is often mandated for the first account opening to satisfy the 'know your customer' (KYC) requirements under French law (Code Monétaire et Financier).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction volume and rapid turnover in a newly established entity without prior trading history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a comprehensive business plan, audited financial projections, contracts with suppliers and buyers, and evidence of physical commodity storage or logistics arrangements. Include a detailed explanation of the supply chain, source of funds, and expected transaction patterns. Submit corporate registry extracts (Kbis), shareholder structure, and beneficial ownership declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments to/from high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., tax havens or sanctioned countries) for copper procurement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a complete trade documentation trail: purchase orders, invoices, bills of lading, warehouse receipts (LME warrants), and inspection certificates. Provide a compliance certificate confirming the origin of goods and the absence of sanctions exposure. Implement a robust sanctions screening process and provide evidence of due diligence on all counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of complex corporate structures or multiple intermediary entities in the transaction chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Disclose the full corporate structure, including all intermediate holding companies, and provide a rationale for the structure. Submit organizational charts, shareholder agreements, and proof of economic substance for each entity. Ensure that all entities have valid tax registrations and are not shell companies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual payment patterns, such as early settlement or prepayment for goods without corresponding delivery
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a clear explanation of the trade terms (e.g., Incoterms) and payment milestones. Submit the underlying contract and any amendments. Include evidence of the physical movement of goods, such as transport documents and insurance certificates. Maintain a transaction log and reconcile payments with shipments.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections (e.g., shareholder loans or equity contributions) must be routed via SWIFT wire transfers using the appropriate purpose codes. For equity contributions, use the BOP code '110' (Direct investment) or '120' (Capital in cash). For shareholder loans, use '130' (Loans and credits). The transfer must be accompanied by a declaration to the Banque de France via the BOP reporting system within 30 days. The receiving bank will require a copy of the corporate resolution authorizing the injection, the shareholder agreement, and proof of the source of funds. For amounts exceeding EUR 10,000, the bank will conduct enhanced due diligence and may request a certificate of tax residence for the sending entity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for copper cathode purchases are typically executed via SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) for direct payments, or via documentary letters of credit (LC) for larger, more secure transactions. For LCs, the bank will issue an irrevocable LC (MT700) in favor of the seller, with the buyer's bank confirming the LC. The clearing rails involve the correspondent banking network, with settlement in EUR or USD (commonly USD for LME trades). For LME warrant transfers, the payment is often made via MT103 with the warrant transfer instruction separately. All outbound payments must be reported to the Banque de France under the BOP system. The bank will require the underlying trade documents (invoice, bill of lading, inspection certificate) to process the payment and ensure compliance with AML/CTF regulations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward contracts (FX forwards) for EUR/USD and other major currencies, with tenors up to 12 months, available from French banks and international banks with a French presence.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with limited convertibility, though not typically needed for EUR/USD; may be used for exotic currencies if the copper supplier is in a restricted market.
Currency swaps (FX swaps) for managing short-term liquidity and rolling over positions, subject to ISDA agreements and collateral requirements.
Options (FX options) for hedging price volatility, though these are less common for physical commodity traders and may require additional credit lines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of result
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAS shareholders; no public authority filing for the approval itself
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late approval may expose officers to liability and prevent timely accounts filing; no automatic strike-off deadline applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing, including applicable management and corporate governance documents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry through the French one-stop business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval; two months where filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction may be issued; failure to comply can result in a civil fine of up to EUR 1,500, doubled for repeat offenses, plus daily coercive penalties. No fixed automatic strike-off period applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return Form 2065 and financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within three months after year-end; for a 31 December year-end, by the second business day after 1 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing interest and tax surcharges may apply, generally including a 10% surcharge, with higher penalties for persistent or deliberate non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual value-added tax return or annual VAT regularization, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Under the entity's VAT regime: monthly or quarterly CA3 filings, or annual CA12 filing generally within three months after the relevant annual period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest and tax surcharges may apply; inaccurate VAT reporting can trigger reassessment and additional penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by the second business day after 1 May for taxpayers required to file; filing obligation generally applies where turnover exceeds EUR 152,500
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or inaccurate filing may result in administrative penalties and tax reassessment. The tax is subject to statutory phase-out rules and should be checked for the relevant year.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual municipal business property tax (CFE) payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally payable by 15 December; no routine annual renewal filing is normally required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment may generate collection surcharges and interest; enforcement measures may follow unpaid assessments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership information update, where changes occurred
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry through the French one-stop business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any change to beneficial ownership or relevant identification information; no annual confirmation is generally required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to declare or maintain accurate beneficial ownership information may result in court orders, fines, officer liability, and restrictions affecting registration or banking compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally required when the SAS exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Mandatory appointment may also arise under specified control, group, or corporate restructuring circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC) regulations. IFRS may apply to consolidated accounts where legally permitted or required; an unlisted SAS normally uses French GAAP for statutory individual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not generally require an annual beneficial ownership confirmation where no information has changed. Any change must be declared within 30 days. Share transfers must be reflected promptly in the register of movements of securities and the relevant individual securities accounts, subject to the SAS articles and applicable transfer formalities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders or individual securities accounts
Register of shareholders' decisions and minutes
Register of management or corporate officer decisions, where maintained for the SAS
Accounting books and supporting accounting records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 300-1,500 per year, approximately USD 325-1,625, depending on address, mail handling, and administrative services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately EUR 3,000-12,000 per year, or USD 3,250-13,000, for a small or medium-sized SAS; larger, group, or complex trading operations may exceed this range

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax on taxable profits
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to statutory conditions, including turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up share capital, and at least 75% direct or indirect ownership by individuals or qualifying entities. Certain innovation, research, investment, and regional incentives may also apply. The ordinary 25% rate applies above the qualifying reduced-rate band.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, filed electronically through the French tax administration's professional portal at impots.gouv.fr using EDI-TDFC or EFI. The return is accompanied by the tax package, principally Forms 2050-SD to 2059-G-SD.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally within three months after the end of the financial year. For financial years ending on 31 December, the deadline is generally the second business day after 1 May of the following year. The tax administration may publish an annual administrative filing calendar with the operational date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, SIREN number, tax office, financial year dates, legal form, and contact details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French SAS is generally a French tax resident. The foreign shareholder's residence and tax identification details should not replace the SAS's French registered-office and SIREN information.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss transferred from the detailed tax package and reconciliation schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only profits or losses attributable to the French SAS. Do not include the foreign shareholder's unrelated turnover, assets, or tax results.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Extra-accounting additions and deductions, including non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, provisions, depreciation adjustments, and other permanent or temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party charges to non-resident entities must be supported by arm's-length evidence, contractual documentation, benefit analysis, and payment records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carryforwards used in the current year and remaining tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses must be substantiated through prior filed returns and preserved accounting records. A material change in business activity or cessation of the business may restrict use of carried-forward losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital gains, shareholdings, provisions, depreciation, and other tax-specific information required by the tax package.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose foreign related-party holdings and transactions where required. Separate trading inventory from fixed assets and financial investments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base, applicable rates, tax credits, instalments, withholding credits, and balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are available only where permitted by French domestic law or an applicable tax treaty and must be supported by foreign tax payment evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax balance or refund claim.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay any balance electronically. A refund claim must reconcile to the filed return and the French bank account or authorized payment arrangement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Four instalments generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, subject to statutory exceptions and applicable tax thresholds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The payment obligation belongs to the French SAS, regardless of whether its shareholders or parent companies are resident abroad.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, potentially increased to 40% for a deliberate failure after formal notice and 80% in aggravated cases. Late payment generally attracts interest at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules and relief provisions. Incorrect returns may trigger tax reassessment, interest, surcharges, and criminal tax-fraud exposure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2572-SD for the corporate income tax balance and Form 2571-SD for instalment payments, filed or paid electronically through the professional tax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly payments with an annual final balance
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Instalments are generally due on the 15th day of March, June, September, and December. The final balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the usual date is 15 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year corporate income tax instalment based principally on the preceding year's liability or the current year's estimated liability where permitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SAS's own corporate income tax liability and do not offset unrelated foreign taxes or parent-company liabilities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax payable for the completed financial year before crediting instalments and qualifying tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the amount to Form 2065-SD and the tax package.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Instalments paid, tax credits, withholding credits, and other legally available offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim foreign withholding tax as a French credit unless a treaty or domestic provision expressly permits the credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount payable or refundable after all permitted offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain evidence of all payments, credits, and bank instructions, particularly where the French company is controlled by a foreign shareholder.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment may generate 5% recovery surcharges in specified circumstances, late-payment interest at 0.20% per month, enforcement costs, and collection measures. Repeated non-payment may result in tax liens, account seizures, director-management restrictions, or insolvency proceedings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2777-SD for withholding tax on dividends, interest, royalties, and other reportable investment income, filed electronically through the professional tax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally by the 15th day of the month following the month in which the relevant income was paid or made available, subject to the applicable reporting rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classification of dividends, interest, royalties, or other investment income paid to the non-resident recipient.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the recipient's legal name, jurisdiction, tax identification information, beneficial ownership status, and payment date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross amount paid or made available before withholding.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the contractual gross amount and maintain payment instructions, invoices, board approvals, and accounting entries.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Domestic withholding rate or reduced treaty/directive rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply a reduced rate only after obtaining adequate residence, beneficial ownership, eligibility, and anti-abuse documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax collected and remitted to the French tax administration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French SAS remains responsible for correct withholding and payment even where the foreign recipient contractually bears the tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold or remit may result in recovery of the unpaid tax from the French payer, late-payment interest, penalties generally ranging from 10% to 80% depending on the conduct, and potential criminal exposure for fraudulent concealment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Generally 25% on dividends paid by a French company to a non-resident recipient, subject to domestic exemptions, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive as implemented in France, applicable tax treaties, and anti-abuse requirements. A qualifying EU or EEA parent may obtain exemption where statutory ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority, verify beneficial ownership and treaty entitlement, confirm the required ownership and holding-period conditions, and collect any prescribed treaty forms or reduced-rate declarations. The French SAS should retain the residence certificate, ownership chart, board resolutions, agreements, payment evidence, and substance documentation. If relief is unavailable at source, the recipient may generally seek a refund through the applicable French claim procedure. Treaty relief is jurisdiction-specific and cannot be determined without the recipient's country of residence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by a French resident to a non-resident are generally subject to French withholding at the domestic rate applicable to the payment, commonly 25%, subject to treaty reduction, EU directive relief, and anti-abuse rules. Interest paid to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding under ordinary domestic rules, except for specific statutory cases, including certain payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions or territories, for which a higher rate may apply. Treaty rates depend on the recipient's jurisdiction, beneficial ownership, instrument, and applicable treaty article. Related-party financing must also satisfy arm's-length pricing, debt-capacity, interest-limitation, and anti-hybrid rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A French entity is generally subject to full transfer-pricing documentation requirements where its turnover or gross assets are at least EUR 400 million, or where it belongs to a group meeting the statutory conditions. A transfer-pricing declaration is generally required for entities meeting the EUR 50 million turnover or gross-assets threshold or other statutory connected-party criteria. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a standalone ESR regime equivalent to the United Arab Emirates or certain offshore jurisdictions. Nevertheless, French anti-abuse rules, the arm's-length principle, beneficial-ownership standards, controlled foreign company rules, interest-limitation rules, anti-hybrid rules, principal-purpose testing, general anti-abuse provisions, and EU ATAD measures require genuine commercial rationale and adequate substance. A French copper-trading SAS should maintain French decision-making, transaction-control functions, qualified personnel or outsourced operational capacity, inventory and logistics evidence, treasury controls, customer and supplier due diligence, and records demonstrating that its margin reflects functions, assets, and risks actually assumed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing copper sales, omitting taxable revenue, fabricating purchase invoices, misclassifying private expenditure, creating false losses, or using sham transactions to reduce French corporate income tax or VAT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, repayment of tax, late-payment interest, and penalties generally up to 80% in aggravated cases. Criminal tax fraud may result in imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, with higher sanctions for aggravated or organized conduct, including imprisonment of up to seven years and fines of up to EUR 3 million in qualifying cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal prosecution, civil tax-liability proceedings for fraudulent or repeated non-payment, management bans, asset seizure, and restitution. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may be imposed through judicial measures in appropriate proceedings. The corporate veil is not routinely pierced; personal exposure generally requires personal participation, serious management fault, fraud, or statutory director-liability grounds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: VAT carousel fraud and missing-trader arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using conduit companies to obtain fraudulent VAT refunds, claiming input VAT on fictitious copper purchases, circulating invoices without genuine movement of goods, or participating in intra-EU transactions designed to conceal the missing trader.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, denial of input-tax recovery, interest, penalties up to 80% for fraudulent conduct, joint and several recovery in qualifying circumstances, and criminal sanctions for organized fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may incur criminal liability, personal tax-liability orders for serious management misconduct, asset freezes, professional disqualification, and imprisonment where they knowingly participated in the scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's-length purchase or resale prices, unsupported management fees, artificial financing charges, profit diversion, or contractual arrangements inconsistent with the actual functions and risks of the French SAS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable profits, denial of deductions, withholding-tax exposure, documentation penalties, late-payment interest, and penalties generally ranging from 10% to 80% depending on the taxpayer's conduct and the degree of concealment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability may arise for deliberate participation, fraudulent bookkeeping, or serious management misconduct. Directors should approve and retain contemporaneous benchmarking, intercompany agreements, functional analyses, and transaction-level evidence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using nominee shareholders, undisclosed beneficial owners, circular ownership, fictitious directors, sham offices, or offshore entities to conceal control, divert profits, or defeat tax and sanctions screening.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment under anti-abuse principles, beneficial-owner and corporate-register sanctions, account freezing, contract termination, AML reporting, and potential criminal penalties for fraud, money laundering, or false corporate declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, de facto managers, and beneficial owners may face criminal prosecution, asset confiscation, management bans, civil restitution, and imprisonment. Travel bans may be ordered by a court where legally justified.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-money laundering, terrorist financing, and sanctions violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, dealing with sanctioned persons or entities, bypassing KYC controls, concealing the source of copper-trade funds, using opaque payment chains, or processing suspicious documentary letters of credit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Suspicious transaction reporting, account restrictions, regulatory enforcement, administrative fines, confiscation, and criminal sanctions. Sanctions and export-control breaches may also cause contractual termination, banking de-risking, and loss of market access.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may incur criminal and regulatory liability for knowing participation or serious control failures, including fines, imprisonment where applicable, professional bans, asset seizure, and judicial travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording nonexistent inventory, falsifying LME warrant transfers, manipulating copper grades or weights, backdating invoices, disguising related-party transactions, or creating false transport and customs documents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Accounting corrections, tax reassessment, civil damages, commercial penalties, and criminal prosecution for forgery, use of forged documents, fraud, or fraudulent accounting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president, managing officers, beneficial owners, accountants, and other participants may face individual criminal liability, fines, imprisonment, asset confiscation, management bans, and civil restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misdeclaring origin, customs value, tariff classification, quantity, or importer of record; using false certificates; or evading customs duties and import VAT on copper cathodes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of duties and import VAT, customs fines, seizure or forfeiture of goods, customs investigation, and criminal prosecution in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Company officers and persons directing the transaction may face personal customs liability, criminal fines, imprisonment in serious cases, asset seizure, and restrictions on managing companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal dividend distribution and unlawful profit extraction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends without distributable profits, extracting funds through sham loans or undocumented expenses, paying dividends while insolvent, or failing to account for dividend withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of unlawful dividends, director liability, corporate-law penalties, tax reassessment, withholding-tax recovery, interest, and penalties. Insolvency-related claims may include clawback and mismanagement actions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be required to restore misappropriated amounts, compensate creditors, bear insolvency liabilities for serious management faults, and face criminal sanctions for abuse of corporate assets or fraudulent bankruptcy.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Continuing to trade while insolvent, preferring related parties, transferring inventory or cash below market value, destroying records, or moving assets offshore before creditor enforcement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Clawback of transactions, insolvency proceedings, personal contribution to liabilities, director-management bans, and criminal bankruptcy sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president and de facto managers may face civil contribution claims, asset seizure, management prohibitions, criminal fines, and imprisonment for fraudulent bankruptcy or asset dissipation.
